added_failures_note: The reviewed run is a read-only recon node whose declared write paths reach no test path. Its manifest records baseline_suite and after_suite as JSON null (classification.json confirms both null) and negative_control_log as 'none' with a reason, so there are no gate suite logs to difference. The derived delta is therefore zero: no head arm exists that could add a failing id over a base arm, so added_failure_count is 0 and added_failure_ids is []. This is not a claim that a suite passed; the armed-suite measure does not apply to a read-only evidence node. The node's own declared control (an equilibrium is reported only where an E101154 EQDB index lists a slice, and every index and EDDB category was probed rather than assumed) is a reproduction discipline, not an executable guard, so there is no red log and none is required.

findings.text: follow-on: the fragment quotes the Fortran socket entry as eqdbio_rev.f 'call SOCKET_EQDBIO(3, ...)'. The reviewed run's own transcript (recon7.log) shows the actual call sites pass a variable: eqdbio_rev.f:125/184/211/218 each read 'call SOCKET_EQDBIO( eqtyp, code, sshot, ttime, irev, ...)'. The literal 3 is the get/put/update/remove selector value documented in eqdbio.f ('= 3 : update the EQDB data'), not the argument at any call site shown. The neighbouring SOCKET_EQDBLIST quote (eqdb_get_rev.f:163 'call SOCKET_EQDBLIST(1, s_shot, listwk, nlistwk, errcd)') is exact. Because the done-when asks the node to quote the call, one of its two quoted call lines should show the real argument list.

follow-on: the selene subpackage list names 'eftout' among the record readers. No such module exists; the file is selene/efitout.py (recon12.log lists /analysis/src/edas2/v2.2.1/edas_share/eqread_pac/selene/efitout.py), and the reviewed run's own reasoning text calls it 'efitout'. A reader grepping the package for 'eftout' finds nothing.

follow-on: the fields table's 'unit' column carries quantity meanings where units belong for the profile group -- the SIV/VLV/QQV/PRV/BTV row lists 'psi, V, q, mu0P, F=R·B_T', which identify what each array is, not its unit -- and the boundary row (line 116) gives CSU the unit 'A/m^2', which no quoted source line supports (the FAME COMMON block declares CSU_BF(ISRZDM_BF) with no unit, and the run's own notes give CSU no unit). PSI/RG/ZG/RAXIS/ZAXIS/SAXIS/TTCU/EQTIM units are grounded in the reader NameList and the COMMON block names. The column heading and its contents disagree for five fields.

follow-on: the done-when asks the fragment to list the record's fields 'with shapes and units read from one E101154 time slice'. No slice could be read: GetEqData(0,101154,500) returns IRET 300 and every field reads back shape (0,), reproduced in recon13.log. The fragment states this honestly and sources the shapes and units from the reader schema (Fledd.py NameList) and the FAME COMMON blocks, not from a values dump. The value-level read therefore remains unattempted-as-met and is carried forward for the transport/loader node, exactly as the predecessor jtmm-eqdb-entry-probe's review already recorded. Not the node's fault -- the cause is the unmounted FAME server -- but the done-when's slice clause is not satisfied.

justifications.durability: This is a read-only evidence node: its write paths reach no test path, so it adds no automated test and can add none; the manifest records negative_control_log as 'none' with a reason and baseline_suite/after_suite as null, and classification.json agrees. Durability therefore rests on the finding being re-derivable. It is only partly. The thirteen recon transcripts are retained in the run directory and are what I read to reproduce every number, so the evidence is preserved. But the finding is a negative about a remote facility, dependent on the SELENE run tree and the EQDB index listings of one shot on one date, and nothing in the repository fails if the situation changes -- if SELENE's E101154 equilibrium is later produced, or the FAME server is mounted, no test or guard records that this conclusion was provisional. The probe scripts are not in the repository (read-only node), so a reader of the repo alone cannot re-run them. The declared control is a prose rule, not an executable check. Deduction for the absent durable instrument and the perishable remote-state dependency.
justifications.evidence: The principal measured claims reproduce from the run's own recon transcripts. I read recon1..recon13 and confirmed, independently of the fragment: the EQDB index sweep returns 0 slices for every EQDB index except eqdb=0, which returns 105 (recon6.log, and recon13.log GetTimeList(0,101154) first five 500/800/900/1000/1100); eqdball 1 -s 101154 and eqdb -s 101154 print '* No DATA *' while eqdball 0 -s 101154 lists 000500.. (recon10.log); the EDDB catalogue is 73 categories with 'FAME' present and no 'SELENE' (recon12.log catTable, count 73), and every candidate category read returns irc=1022 (recon11.log); the SELENE run tree holds EFIT95.DATA (293630 B, Jan 8 2021), EQSLE.DATA, fort.95, fort.96, run, sel and no E101154 file (recon5.log), and the bounded finds return only ~/work/efit_jt60sa/E101154_signals.npz; eqdbget.f declares NEQDB1=MOD(NEQDB,100) and CALL ALLEQDBIO(NEQDB1,1,ISH,ITIME,IRET,0) and the COMMON block sizes IRDM_BF=129/IZDM_BF=65/IVDM_BF=51/IZDM2_BF=129 (recon9.log); libEQDBMSPIC.so exports eqdbsockclient_connect and siblings (recon7.log nm, recon8.log strings); dbsvr17p has no DNS and port 22 is closed/filtered (recon8.log); GetEqData(0,101154,500) returns IRET 300 with the library line 'eqtyp, code, sshot, ttime = 0 1 101154 500' and all fields shape (0,) (recon13.log). Three accuracy defects dock this dimension: the socket call is quoted as SOCKET_EQDBIO(3, ...) when the sources pass a variable (finding 1), the module is written 'eftout' for efitout (finding 2, scope: fit), and the unit column mixes quantity meanings with units and states an unsourced 'A/m^2' for CSU (finding 3). The overall finding is nevertheless well-evidenced: every number I could check reproduces.
justifications.fit: A clean evidence fragment: bare reckon fragment section, node-prefixed element ids, a location list with the command and its return per candidate, a reader paragraph, a fields table, and a socket-test paragraph. The commit is conventional with a body (docs(evidence): ...), states what changed and why, and carries no plan/sprint/ticket identifier and no AI attribution. Naming is by mechanism (eqdb index, eqdbms, eqdbsockclient_connect). Deductions: the 'eftout' typo (finding 2); the unit column conflates quantities and units (finding 3, joint with evidence); and one sentence is garbled -- line 26-27 reads 'eqdb_path_put prints the default root /JT60SA... as /JT60SA_EQ/EQDB (return 0)', where the ellipsis and the words 'default root' do not parse and the useful fact (the binary eqdb_path_put returns /JT60SA_EQ/EQDB, rc=0, recon10.log) is buried.
justifications.goal_fidelity: Plan section 6's brief for jtmm-selene-output-locate (docs/plans/jt60sa-machine-map.html, section 6: find where SELENE's plasma-shape run stores its equilibrium for E101154 -- an EDDB category, an EQDB index other than eqdbms, or a file tree under the run directory -- name the reader that consumes it, and test whether a FAME record reads through the EQDB socket client eqdbsockclient_connect from intr26-2) is answered, but as a negative. The fragment reports that no SELENE equilibrium for E101154 exists in any of the three named places: the DEFAULT EQDB index (eqdb=1, EQDB_PATH /JT60SA_EQ/EQDB) lists no slice (eqdball 1 -s 101154 and eqdb -s 101154 both print '* No DATA *'), a reader sweep GetTimeList(eqdb,101154) over eqdb=-3..8 returns 0 everywhere except eqdb=0 (105 slices), the 73-category EDDB catalogue has FAME but no SELENE category and every candidate category read returns irc=1022, and the SELENE run tree /analysis/src/SAselene_v2.0_forPSRC/RUN/ holds one stale January-2021 run (EFIT95.DATA 293630 B) with no per-shot E101154 output (E101154 is a December-2023 shot). The only reachable E101154 equilibrium record is FAME's EQDB index eqdb=0 -- an EQDB index other than eqdbms -- and the fragment names its reader and its fields and tests the socket path. Two deductions. First, the done-when's clause 'with shapes and units read from one E101154 time slice' is unmet: the read fails (IRET 300) so the fields are the declared schema, as the fragment itself says (finding 4). Second, the fragment does not surface plainly that it shows the plan's premise -- that SELENE's plasma-shape equilibrium for E101154 exists -- to be unsupported for this shot; the implication paragraph says the record 'does not exist for E101154', which is the right call, but the answer to the assigned question is a negative rather than the positive location the done-when's parenthetical anticipates. The reconstruction work the plan wanted (a named SELENE record to bind) is not available for E101154.
justifications.reuse: The node reuses the shipped reader rather than building a parallel one: it probes through the same eqread_pac package (db/FleddTool.py) and the same Fortran FAME reader eqdbget.f that the predecessor jtmm-eqdb-entry-probe identified, and it adds no source, no second reader, and no new operator, consistent with a read-only recon node. The socket finding is anchored to the prebuilt libEQDBMSPIC.so symbols and the client_eqdbms reverse-reader sources rather than to a reimplementation. There is no in-repo call site because the node writes only a fragment. It does not, however, close the loop with the predecessor's schema -- it restates the field list independently rather than citing jtmm-eqdb-entry-probe, so a reader finds two field tables (this fragment's and the predecessor's) with the small divergences noted in finding 3. Reuse is high; the deduction is for the missed cross-reference, not for any duplicated instrument.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff d2bb8d08..3155a7e4 touches exactly one file: docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-machine-map/jtmm-selene-output-locate.html (177 insertions, one commit 3155a7e4). That is the first of the two declared write paths; the declared figure directory docs/figures/jt60sa-machine-map/jtmm-selene-output-locate is unused, which is consistent -- the done-when names no artifact and the plan says the node writes one evidence fragment. No source under imas_ambix/, no scripts/, no tests/, and no plan edit is touched. Base d2bb8d08 matches the manifest's orientation_base_sha. The fragment is a bare <section data-reckon="fragment"> with all element ids prefixed jtmm-selene-output-locate, matching the sibling jtmm-eqdb-entry-probe.html. The probe was read-only on nakasvr26 (stated: nothing written outside /tmp, one ssh connection at a time via ssh -F ~/.ssh/config jt-60sa), and the manifest carries no uncommitted work; the worktree is clean.

negative_control.mutation: report an equilibrium location for E101173, on which SELENE did not run
negative_control.note: The reviewed run's write paths reach no test path, so no red log was produced and none is required (its manifest records negative_control_log as 'none: ...'). I could not independently exercise the mutation, because it is stated in prose rather than implemented as a check, and the dataset it turns on (EQDB index listings for a shot on nakasvr26) is reachable only over an intermittent IFERC VPN from the login node. What I could verify independently is the observation the guard rests on: the reviewed run's own transcripts swept every EQDB index through the reader and found a slice list for eqdb=0 only, so the rule 'report a location only where an index lists a slice' is the rule that would have refused E101173, whose SELENE index also lists nothing. The control is therefore non-vacuous but unverified as an executable refusal.

Independent review of node jtmm-selene-output-locate (plan imas-ambix:jt60sa-machine-map section 6), read at head 3155a7e48288ea97c21bc10382f7fdf0b739396d on base d2bb8d081559ca088c2d44e74f06416584f956dc.
Read: the single commit 3155a7e4 against base (the fragment, 177 insertions), the committed fragment at head, the run's manifest and classification.json, the plan section 6 text and the eqdb-reader open question, and the run's recon1..recon13 transcripts.
Reproduced independently from the run's own transcripts: the EQDB index sweep returns a slice list for eqdb=0 only (105 slices, 500..11500 ms), 0 for eqdb=-3..8 otherwise (recon6, recon13); eqdball 1 -s 101154 and eqdb -s 101154 print '* No DATA *' (recon10); the EDDB catalogue is 73 categories with FAME present and no SELENE, and every candidate category read returns irc=1022 (recon11, recon12); the SELENE run tree holds one stale January-2021 run and no E101154 output, and the bounded finds return only E101154_signals.npz (recon5); eqdbget.f declares NEQDB1=MOD(NEQDB,100) and CALL ALLEQDBIO(NEQDB1,1,ISH,ITIME,IRET,0) with COMMON sizes 129/65/51 (recon9); libEQDBMSPIC.so exports eqdbsockclient_connect (recon7, recon8); dbsvr17p has no DNS and port 22 closed/filtered (recon8); GetEqData(0,101154,500) returns IRET 300 with the library line 'eqtyp, code, sshot, ttime = 0 1 101154 500' and all fields shape (0,) (recon13).
Scope: the single commit touches only the fragment; no base/head suite arms exist (read-only node), so added_failure_count is 0.
Defects: the socket call is quoted as SOCKET_EQDBIO(3, ...) where the sources pass a variable eqtyp (recon7); the selene reader is written 'eftout' for efitout; the fields table's unit column mixes quantity meanings with units (SIV/VLV/QQV/PRV/BTV) and gives CSU an unsourced 'A/m^2' unit; and the done-when's 'read from one E101154 time slice' clause is unmet (IRET 300).
